The Terms of Service are for the Tumblr service. Here's a plain-language summary:

**Key Provisions:**

* The Terms of Service govern your relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You own your content on Tumblr, but by using the service, you grant Tumblr a license to use your content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms cross-reference Tumblr's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data the company collects and how it processes it.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will be resolved through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Class-action lawsuits are waived under these terms.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, but the conditions for termination are only available in the live document.

**Key Considerations:**

* When you share your content publicly on Tumblr, it may be used by AI partners (e.g., for training) and there's no opt-out for private accounts.
* The Terms allow Tumblr to use your content in various ways, which may include training its AI/ML systems.
* The dispute resolution process involves binding arbitration, which can be less favorable to the user than going to court.
* Class-action lawsuits are waived, which may limit your options if many users are affected by a similar issue.

**Concerns:**

* The use of public content for AI training without an opt-out for private accounts may raise concerns for users who don't want their content used in this way.
* The binding arbitration process and waiver of class-action lawsuits may limit user rights.

Remember that these Terms of Service are subject to change, and it's essential to review the current Terms whenever you use the service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

**Service Name:** Canva Terms of Use

The Canva Terms of Use is a set of rules that govern your relationship with Canva and how you use their products and services. Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These Terms apply to the products and services described on Canva's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** Canva uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI and machine learning (AI/ML) systems, subject to your settings and the law.
* **Generative AI Tools (Magic Studio):** When using Canva's AI tools, you own the output, but there are restrictions on using the generated content to train other AI models. Canva also has content-moderation and labeling requirements.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference Canva's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You're required to participate in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. However, this clause is waived for Canva's relationship with Steam (Valve).
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact:** If you have questions, contact Canva through the published legal contact information on their website.

**Clauses that May be Harmful to the User:**

* **Content and License:** Be aware that Canva has the right to use your submitted content for various purposes, including training its AI/ML systems. While Canva will respect your settings and applicable law, this clause may raise concerns about data ownership and control.
* **Generative AI Tools (Magic Studio):** The restriction on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models might limit your ability to repurpose the output for certain purposes.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver may limit your ability to participate in collective lawsuits or class actions.

Please note that these clauses are not necessarily "harmful" but rather should be carefully read and considered by users before agreeing to the Terms of Service.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

**Service Name:** Stack Overflow Public Network Terms of Service

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline the rules and responsibilities between you, the user, and Stack Overflow. They explain how user-submitted content is used, stored, and protected. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The Terms cover your relationship with Stack Overflow and its products and services.
* **Content and License:** You retain ownership of user-submitted content, but by posting it, you're licensing it under Creative Commons (CC BY-SA). However, Stack Overflow limits bulk extraction of content for AI training without a commercial agreement. This means they won't let you use a lot of their content to train your own AI without discussing it with them first.
* **Privacy:** The Terms reference Stack Overflow's published Privacy Policy, which explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The Terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means you can't join a group lawsuit against Stack Overflow. However, you have a 30-day window to opt out of this process when you first create an account. (Note: Steam, one of their competitors, has removed mandatory arbitration.)
* **Termination:** Either you or Stack Overflow can terminate the agreement, but you'll need to follow the conditions outlined in the live document.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about the Terms, you can check the company's published legal contact information on their website.

**Potential Harm:**

* **Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers:** This clause might limit your ability to seek redress for any grievances you have against Stack Overflow.
* **Termination:** Without knowing the specific conditions outlined in the live document, it's unclear what circumstances would trigger termination, which could leave you without access to your account or data.

**Additional Notes:**

* Stack Overflow has content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google, which might affect how their AI/ML systems are trained and used.
* The 30-day opt-out window for arbitration might be a concern for users who don't want to give up their right to join a class-action lawsuit.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

**Summary of 23andMe Terms of Service:**

23andMe is a genetic testing and health services company. The Terms of Service document governs your relationship with 23andMe.

**Key Provisions:**

* **What's Covered:** The terms apply to the products and services offered by 23andMe, as listed on their official terms page.
* **User Content:** 23andMe will use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Data Protection:** 23andMe will process your personal data as outlined in their published Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with 23andMe, you and they will use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) instead of going to court. You must opt out within 30 days of opening your account.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement under certain conditions.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

The key document is Twitch's Terms of Service. 

Here's a summary of its main provisions:

- **Scope:** The Terms of Service define Twitch users' relationships with the platform, covering its products and services.
  
**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License**: You retain ownership of your content, but you grant Twitch a license to use it on the platform. They may also use it to train AI systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Twitch will collect personal data, as described in their Privacy Policy, which is accessible from the Terms of Service.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most users are required to use binding arbitration and can avoid in-class actions for 30 days after opening a new account.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement according to the conditions set in the document.

**Clauses You Should Be Aware Of:**

* **Dispute Resolution (Binding Arbitration)**: Under the Terms of Service, disputes will be decided through binding arbitration, instead of a court trial. While this is common in many contracts, some users might find the lack of a trial option limiting.
  
In summary, when using Twitch, you grant them a license to use your content, and agree to their privacy practices. Understand how your content is used to train AI.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .

**Service Name:** Roblox Terms of Use

**Overview:** These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you (the user) and Roblox, a platform for creating and sharing online experiences. By agreeing to these terms, you're allowing Roblox to use your content to improve its products and services, while also governing how you interact with the platform.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the services and products described on Roblox's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** If you submit content to Roblox, you're allowing the company to use it to operate, improve, and train its AI and ML systems, as per your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference Roblox's published Privacy Policy, which outlines what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Disputes may be settled through binding arbitration, which means a private process instead of going to court. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** You or Roblox can terminate the agreement subject to the conditions outlined in the document.

**Potential Concerns for Users:**

* **Arbitration Class-Waiver:** Roblox requires binding arbitration with a class-action waiver, which means you give up the right to participate in a group lawsuit if you have a similar issue with Roblox. This can be seen as limiting your rights as a user.
* **Data Use:** The terms allow Roblox to use your submitted content and possibly even your personal data to train its AI and ML systems, which might be concerning if you're not comfortable with that level of data sharing.
* **Potential Termination:** The terms give Roblox the right to terminate the agreement, which might leave you without access to your account or content.

**Important Contacts:** If you have questions about the Terms of Service, you can find contact information on Roblox's help page. The previous version of the Terms of Service is available for historical reference at the provided URL.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EPIC GAMES TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised the Fortnite/Epic Account language, added User-Generated Content (UEFN) provisions and creator-payout rules, updated EU-specific consumer-rights language post-DMA, and refreshed dispute-resolution sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Epic Games to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

**Service Name:** DoorDash Consumer Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with DoorDash when using their products and services.
* **Content and License:** When you use DoorDash, you grant the company permission to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. (This means they might use information you share on their platform to improve their services.)
* **Privacy:** Your personal data is processed in accordance with DoorDash's Privacy Policy. (This means they have a separate policy that explains what data they collect and how they use it.)
* **Dispute Resolution:** In case of disputes, DoorDash requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. There is a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions or concerns, you can refer to DoorDash's published legal contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Binding arbitration with class-action waivers:** This means you may not be able to join a class-action lawsuit if you experience similar issues with DoorDash's services. This could limit your ability to seek compensation or hold DoorDash accountable for any wrongdoing.
* **Use of user-submitted content:** While DoorDash uses your content to improve their services, there is no clear guarantee that they will keep your content confidential or delete it once it's been used.
* **Termination on condition:** The terms don't clearly outline specific conditions that would lead to termination, which could leave you uncertain about when your account might be terminated.

It's essential to note that the Terms of Service are subject to change, and the new version includes updates related to arbitration, auto-renewal clarifications, tipping and refund mechanics, AI-generated menu summaries, and order-suggestion features.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DOORDASH CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with DoorDash and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration provisions (including mass-arbitration handling), added DashPass auto-renewal clarifications, updated tipping/refund mechanics and added new sections covering AI-generated menu summaries and order-suggestion features.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by DoorDash to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service .

response:
**Cloudflare Self-Serve Subscription Agreement**

These are the terms of service for Cloudflare's subscription-based products and services. The key provisions can be broken down into the following areas:

* **Scope and Relationship**: These terms govern how Cloudflare works with customers, including the products and services offered.
* **Content and Usage**: User-submitted content can be used by Cloudflare to operate, improve, and train AI/ML systems. The terms outline how this happens within the user's settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Cloudflare's published Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most customers are required to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (notably, Steam (Valve) is an exception).
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions outlined in the document.
* **Contact**: Questions about the terms can be directed to Cloudflare's published legal contact information.

**Key Notes and Potential User Risks**:

* The terms do not provide an alternative dispute resolution mechanism for users with disabilities, which may lead to issues in accessing the arbitration process.
* The use of AI Gateway and Workers AI may lead to the collection and processing of user data without explicit consent, potentially raising concerns among users about data ownership and control.
* Users may need to carefully review and adjust their settings to ensure control over how their content is used by Cloudflare's AI/ML systems.

**Additional Resources**:

* For questions about these terms, see Cloudflare's published legal contact information at [https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/](https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/).
* A link to the previous version of the terms is also available at [https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/](https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/).
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CLOUDFLARE SELF-SERVE SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Cloudflare and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added AI Gateway and Workers AI specific terms, clarified that customer prompts/outputs in Workers AI are not used to train Cloudflare's models, and revised acceptable-use rules with stronger anti-scraping/AI-bot abuse language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Cloudflare to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/ .

The Terms of Service is for Stripe Services Agreement (US).

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These terms apply to your relationship with Stripe and its products and services, which you can find on Stripe's official terms page.
2. **Content and License**: When you provide content to Stripe, we might use it to operate, improve, or train our AI/ML systems, but only in accordance with your settings and the law.
3. **Privacy**: Your personal data is protected under Stripe's published Privacy Policy, which explains what data we collect and how we process it.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: Most clauses require binding arbitration, meaning you'll resolve disputes privately instead of in court, with some exceptions (e.g., if you opt out within 30 days or if you have an account through Steam).
5. **Termination**: Either you or Stripe can terminate the agreement, but we'll follow the conditions outlined in the Terms of Service.
6. **Contact**: For questions about these terms, check Stripe's published legal contact information.

**Things to Consider:**

* Binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) might be problematic for some users, as it can limit your ability to seek public justice or join a class-action lawsuit.
* Optional opt-out windows for new accounts, which might not apply to existing users or other types of accounts (e.g., Steam).
* The way Stripe uses user-submitted content, although this is framed as "subject to your settings and applicable law."
* The Termination section might not specify what happens to your data after an account is closed.

Please note that these are just observations and not subjective advice. The Terms of Service do not address questions like:

* How Stripe prioritizes your data protection compared to its commercial interests.
* What happens in the case of a system outage or data breach.
* What specific activities are prohibited under the Terms of Service.

If you have further questions or concerns, you can review Stripe's complete Terms of Service (available at the specified link).
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STRIPE SERVICES AGREEMENT (US) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stripe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised Connect platform-onboarding obligations, added Stripe Radar/AI-fraud-prevention provisions, refreshed dispute and chargeback handling sections, and updated indemnification and liability caps.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stripe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stripe.com/legal/ssa .

response:
[DELTA BULLETS]
- The license to use your content is now perpetual, irrevocable, and can be modified or used for advertising, in addition to display.
- You can no longer participate in class actions when disputes are resolved by arbitration.
- We now retain account data for 36 months after account deletion, instead of the previous 18 months.
- We are no longer required to email registered users 30 days before making material changes to the Terms.
- Continued use of the service after a change is made to the Terms now constitutes acceptance of the new terms.

[NARRATIVE]
The Terms of Service have undergone some changes. Here are the notable updates:

* The license to use your content has been expanded. Previously, you granted ChirpSocial a worldwide, royalty-free license to display content you post. Now, you grant us a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use, distribute, modify, and create derivative works from content you post. This means we have more freedom with your content, especially for advertising purposes.
* We now retain account data for 36 months after account deletion, which is 18 more months than previously.
* The arbitration clause has changed to prevent you from participating in class actions. This means if there's a dispute, you'll have to use private arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), but you can't join a larger group lawsuit.

Some users may find these changes concerning, especially regarding the expanded license and increased data retention period. However, these changes are part of the updated Terms of Service, which you can opt out of by deleting your account. 

The Terms of Service now state that continued use of the service after a change is made to the Terms constitutes acceptance of the new terms. This means you're considered to agree to the updated Terms by keeping your account active.

It's essential to review the updated Terms of Service on your own to understand these changes and how they may affect you.
source_tos:
1. ACCOUNT. By creating an account on ChirpSocial you agree to these Terms.
2. CONTENT LICENSE. You grant ChirpSocial a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use, distribute, modify, and create derivative works from content you post, including for advertising.
3. DATA RETENTION. We retain account data for 36 months after account deletion.
4. ARBITRATION. Disputes are resolved by binding arbitration. You waive the right to participate in any class action.
5. CHANGES. We may modify these Terms at any time. Continued use constitutes acceptance.

[MATERIAL CHANGES]
- Content license expanded from display-only royalty-free to perpetual, irrevocable, including modification, derivative works, and advertising use.
- Data retention after deletion increased from 18 months to 36 months.
- Arbitration clause now adds a class-action waiver (previously not waived).
- Change-of-terms notice removed: previously 30 days' email notice required, now changes take effect via continued use without notice.
[CHANGES TO IGNORE]
- Section 1 wording is identical.

[DELTA BULLETS]
- The time period for sales to be final is reduced from 14 days to 7 days.
- Previously, returned items received a full refund; now, they are only eligible for store credit.
- The payment option has been expanded to include ShopFast Pay, but PayPal and other options are still available.
- The wording regarding the sharing of purchase history with marketing partners has been simplified.
- Opt-out for the sharing of purchase history is no longer universally available, but is limited to users in the EU.

[NARRATIVE]
Let's break down the changes.

The time period for sales to be final has been reduced from 14 days to only 7 days after delivery. This means that if you're not completely satisfied with your purchase, you'll only have 7 days to return or request a refund.

Item returns have also undergone a change. Previously, you could return items within 14 days for a full refund. However, this version adds that items are now only eligible for store credit, which may not be what you were hoping for.

The payment options have expanded to include ShopFast Pay, but it's still unclear how this compare to the existing payment methods like Visa, MasterCard, and PayPal. If you're used to only using certain payment methods, ShopFast Pay might be a new, potentially unfamiliar option.

Lastly, the current policy around sharing your purchase history with marketing partners has been simplified. It's still happening, but the wording is easier to understand. Unfortunately, the ability to opt-out of this sharing has been limited specifically to users in the EU.

It's worth noting that the Terms of Service don't mention any new clauses that explicitly harm you. However, the changes in the return policy and the reduced time period for sales to be final might not be in your favor.

Here are the key points to remember:

* The return policy has changed, so you may only receive store credit instead of a full refund.
* You'll have less time (7 days instead of 14) to ask for a refund or return an item after delivery.
* ShopFast Pay is a new payment option.
* You can still use Visa, MasterCard, PayPal, or ShopFast Pay for payment.
* Privacy: The sharing of your purchase history with marketing partners is still happening, but you can opt-out only if you're a user in the EU.

response:
[DELTA BULLETS]
- The effective date of the Terms of Service has been updated from 2023 to 2024.
- External Microsoft policy pages with moderation details can now be accessed through the Moderation section.
- Third-party platforms hosting Xbox titles may track and share user data under their own terms.
- Family-settings features for kids on Xbox are not guaranteed to be available on third-party platforms.

[NARRATIVE]
The Terms of Service have been updated for 2024. Let's go over what changed:

The most notable change is the addition of a link to an external Microsoft policy page for moderation and enforcement in the section called "MODERATION". This adds more detail to the rules governing moderation.

Under the "XBOX" section, there's a new disclosure: third-party platforms hosting Xbox titles may track and share user data, which is subject to those platforms' own terms. This means that when you use Xbox titles on other people's platforms, you're not only bound by Microsoft's terms, but also by the terms of the platform hosting the content.

Another change in the "XBOX" section is a clarification regarding family-settings features. While these features were previously guaranteed to be available when using Xbox products, the 2024 version notes that they "may not be available" on third-party platforms.

To be specific, here are the key changes:
* **MODERATION**: Added link to external policy page.
* **XBOX**: Third-party platforms may track and share data (under their terms).
* **KIDS ON XBOX**: Family settings features are not guaranteed on third-party platforms.

For users of Xbox titles on third-party platforms, these changes may introduce new considerations regarding data tracking and sharing, as well as limitations on available family settings features.

4. KIDS ON XBOX. Clarifies that family-settings features may not be available on third-party platforms.

[DELTA BULLETS]
- The scope now explicitly includes Claude apps, whereas before it only covered Claude.ai and Claude Pro.
- Enterprise linking accounts now require notice before linking, especially for employer-owned email domains.
- The reference to the Acceptable Use Policy is now stronger, likely indicating it is more accessible or more prominent.
- The dispute resolution sections have been updated, although the extent of the change is unclear.

[NARRATIVE]
The new version of the Terms of Service expands the scope of what's covered, including Claude apps explicitly, whereas before it only covered Claude.ai and Claude Pro. This means you're now agreeing to follow the Terms of Service when using Claude apps as well.

Another notable change is in the Enterprise Linking section. Before, the language was limited, but now it requires notice before linking accounts created with employer-owned email domains. This means you'll likely receive a notification before an account is automatically linked to a Claude account.

The Acceptable Use Policy clause has been strengthened, but the text doesn't clarify what this means in practical terms. It might indicate that this policy is now more accessible or prominent.

Lastly, the dispute resolution sections have been updated, which means there may be changes to how disagreements are resolved. However, the extent of the change is unclear.

As for any potential harm, the main concern is the clarification around Enterprise Linking. If you're using a Claude account with an employer-owned email domain, you should be aware that there might be automated linking, which could potentially lead to issues with employer policies or workplace requirements.

- The new Content License now explicitly includes using posts to train machine-learning and generative-AI models.
- The option for users to opt out of AI training is no longer available.
- Third-party data sharing is now allowed based on a license agreement, rather than being limited to partner relationships.
- Twitter, but not Twitter as previously included, now explicitly is covered under broader scope.

[NARRATIVE]
Let me walk you through the key changes in the updated Terms of Service.

**Content License:** The worldwide royalty-free license now explicitly extends to using your posts to train machine-learning and generative-AI models. This means that your posts can be used without your permission to train AI models, which might be a new concern for you.

**AI Training:** The option for you to opt out of having your content used for AI training is gone. Previously, you could choose not to have your content used for this purpose, but now it's automated and not under your control.

**Third-Party Data Sharing:** The way your content can be shared with third parties has changed. Now, it's based on a license agreement, which might open up your content to more parties. This could be a privacy concern for you.

Here are some possible implications of these changes:

* Your posts may be used without your permission to train powerful AI models, potentially for applications you're not aware of or comfortable with. 
* You no longer have control over whether your content is used for AI training.
* Your content may be shared with a broader range of third parties, potentially under less control.

However, it's worth noting that the updated Terms of Service do not **specifically** state that you will be harmed by these changes.

The updated Terms of Service now explicitly mention that they cover "X services," which is broader than the previous scope of "Twitter / X services."

[DELTA BULLETS]
- YouTube now allows non-Partner creators to monetize their videos.
- Facial recognition data from videos cannot be collected.
- Non-U.S. creators must comply with new U.S. tax-withholding obligations.
- The Terms of Service now apply globally, rather than being region-specific.

[NARRATIVE]
The updated version of the Terms of Service adds a few key changes.

YouTube now allows non-Partner creators to monetize their videos. (previously, only Partner creators could monetize).

* YouTube has the right to monetize most videos on the platform, including those of non-Partner creators (**MONETIZATION**).

The updated version also explicitly prohibits collecting facial-recognition data from videos. There's no change on the side of what you can **not** do, just a clarification.

Non-U.S. creators must now comply with new U.S. tax-withholding obligations when receiving payments. This is a new obligation for creators outside the U.S. who previously didn't have to worry about it.

Lastly, the Terms of Service have been globalized to apply to all users worldwide, rather than being region-specific.

With these updates, the key new obligation for non-U.S. creators is the new U.S. tax-withholding requirements. If you're a non-U.S. creator, be aware of the new tax implications.

A new explicit statement has been added that Adobe does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content. This change is found under the clause "AI TRAINING" and seems to be a welcome change for users concerned about AI model privacy.

Additionally, the language used in the Terms has been rewritten in clearer, plain language, making it easier for users to understand. This is a positive change, as it helps to reduce confusion and uncertainty.

Lastly, Adobe has added plain-English summaries of changes alongside the Terms, which is a good practice for transparency.

*No new clauses have been identified as "harming" you*. The most significant change is the revised scope of access to user content, which could be a concern for some users. However, it is essential to note that the exact scope of access is not specified, and more information would be needed to fully understand its implications.

On the whole, these changes appear to be minor and aimed at improving transparency and user experience.

In terms of any potential harm, these changes primarily impact:

* Developers working with large language models: They must now obtain permission from the service before using the data for this purpose.
* You might need to review your integration: If you're using an app that performs bulk extraction, you might need to check with the app developer to see if they need to adjust their permissions or update their process to comply with the new restrictions.

However, it's generally beneficial for users to have these restrictions in place to protect their data.

As for the "new clauses that may harm me," there are no explicitly new clauses that would directly damage you. The updates clarify and strengthen existing rules to provide better protection for your data.

- Ads on 'no ads' / 'ad-free' tiers are now allowed for streaming titles.
- Expanded mass-arbitration procedures are now in place (compared to standard arbitration provisions).
- New and existing subscribers have different effective dates for the agreement.

[NARRATIVE]
Now that the Terms of Service have been updated, let's review the changes.

The main change worth noting is that ads are now allowed on 'no ads' / 'ad-free' tiers for streaming titles. This means that if you're subscribed to one of these tiers, you may still see ads when streaming certain titles. Previously, these tiers were genuinely ad-free.

Another significant change is the introduction of expanded mass-arbitration procedures. This binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) process has been expanded to cover more cases, and it's a response to concerns raised by a wrongful-death case. While the terms don't specify which disputes will be subject to this process, it's worth noting that you may be required to use this process instead of going to court to resolve disputes.

Finally, the effective date for the agreement is now different for new and existing subscribers. It's worth reviewing which dates apply to you.

As for new clauses that may harm you, I'd highlight the introduction of ads on 'no ads' / 'ad-free' tiers, which may affect your viewing experience. The expanded mass-arbitration procedures may also have implications for how disputes are handled, which could potentially be less favorable to consumers.

However, it's worth noting that the Terms of Service don't provide specific information on how these changes may affect you. If you're concerned about any changes, I recommend reviewing the updated Terms of Service carefully and reaching out to Disney+ support for more information.

**Changes compared to the previous version:**

* Ads on 'no ads' / 'ad-free' tiers are now allowed (previously ad-free)
* Expanded mass-arbitration procedures have been introduced (response to wrongful-death case backlash)
* Effective dates for new and existing subscribers are now different

[DELTA BULLETS]
- The scope of the Terms of Service now covers Alexa, Rufus AI, and other AI services, making it broader.
- The NEW version mentions AI-generated outputs and how they interact with the user agreement.
- The NEW version excludes disputes worth $10,000 or less from mandatory arbitration, allowing users the option to use small-claims courts instead.

[NARRATIVE]
Let's walk through the updates to the Terms of Service.

The updated Terms of Service now cover a broader scope, including Alexa, Rufus AI, and other AI services. This means that your interactions with these services will be governed by the Terms, rather than other separate agreements.

Additionally, the new version has references to AI-generated outputs and how they interact with the user agreement. However, there is no mention of any potential harm or risks related to AI-generated outputs.

One notable change is in the Arbitration clause. Previously, it was mandatory binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) for most disputes. Now, disputes worth $10,000 or less are exempt from this requirement, giving you the option to use small-claims courts instead. This change may benefit you if you have a minor dispute that would otherwise be subject to arbitration.

However, it's worth noting that the Arbitration clause still applies to disputes worth more than $10,000. The updated Terms of Service mention this explicitly.

Here are the specific changes:

* **Broader scope**: Covers Alexa, Rufus AI, and other AI services.
* **AI-generated outputs**: New references to their interaction with the user agreement.
* **Arbitration**: Exempts disputes worth $10,000 or less from mandatory arbitration, allowing the option to use small-claims courts.

There are no new clauses that explicitly harm users.

[DELTA BULLETS]
- The OLD version granted a standard license, while the NEW version has an explicit clause permitting the use of public Pin content to train AI/ML models.
- The OLD version had no AI/ML training clauses, while the NEW version includes new AI-training and recommendation/safety clauses.
- The OLD version had standard advertiser/merchant obligations, while the NEW version has updated obligations.
- The OLD version had standard arbitration provisions, while the NEW version has updated provisions.

[NARRATIVE]
Let's review what's changed. The new Terms of Service update how content is used, specifically with AI. Previously, the Terms granted a standard license over public Pin content. Now, the license is the same, but with an **explicit clause** permitting the use of public Pin content to train AI/ML models. This means that public pins can be used to train AI models, which may have implications for your personal data.

Another area that has changed is **Arbitration**. While you can still opt out of arbitration, the updated provisions do so by default, requiring you to notify us in writing within 30 days if you want to withdraw from arbitration. Keep in mind, arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) is typically binding.

Here are the key changes:

* **Content**: Explicit clause for AI/ML model training (may impact your personal data)
* **Arbitration**: Updated provisions that default to arbitration and require opting out within 30 days (binding arbitration)
* **Advertisers**: Updated advertiser/merchant obligations, but these changes are not explicitly stated and could imply more strict rules.
* **AI**: New AI-training and recommendation/safety clauses (not explicitly stated to directly harm users)

When it comes to new clauses that may harm you, the updated Terms of Service don't explicitly state any new clauses that would cause direct harm. However, the AI clause can be seen as a potential concern, as it allows for the use of your public Pin content for training models. If you're concerned about the use of your data for AI training, you may want to exercise caution when creating public Pins.

Please note that, according to the Terms, **you are responsible for any content** you create and share. However, this hasn't changed in the updated version. If you have any specific concerns, I'd be happy to address them case-by-case. 

If you'd like more information about the changes, I can help you explore the new Terms.

[NARRATIVE]
The Terms of Service have been updated, and there are a few key changes. 

In terms of ownership, the update specifies that users own the outputs of Canva's generative-AI tools, subject to platform rights (which means Canva may retain some rights to the work you create). 

There's also a new rule for Canva's Magic Studio, which means you're not allowed to use Canva-generated content to train other AI models.

Additionally, the update includes new moderation rules that require specific content labeling for AI-generated content. This means you'll need to add certain labels to your AI-generated content before uploading it to Canva.

These changes don't seem to introduce any obvious harm. Here are the specific additions:

* New "AI" section in the Terms of Service with restrictions on Magic Studio usage
* New "MODERATION" section with requirements for labeling AI-generated content
* Specific mention of Canva's platform rights in the "OUTPUT OWNERSHIP" section 

However, it's essential to remember that the "AI-generated content is subject to separate content rules" part does restrict your usage options within Canva. The Terms of Service do not address the potential implications or requirements of these "separate content rules" in detail.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

response:
The Terms of Service describe how user-submitted content is used by Reddit. According to the document (in the CONTENT AND LICENSE section), content posted on Reddit is used by the company "to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems" - subject to your settings and applicable law.

This implies that Reddit does use your content, but it does not explicitly state that it owns the posts. However, in a September 2023 update, explicit terms were added confirming Reddit's right to license your content to third parties (including for AI training), meaning they are allowed to pass it on for use elsewhere, possibly under agreements unknown to you.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — REDDIT USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2023; replaces the 2021 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Reddit and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2021 version in the following ways: September 2023 update added explicit terms confirming Reddit's right to license user content to third parties (including for AI training), added new monetization-related provisions and shifted dispute-resolution venue. Reddit publishes prior versions at redditinc.com/policies.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Reddit to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement-september-12-2021 .

[MUST MENTION]
- own
- license
- third parties
- Google
- OpenAI

user_input: If I want my public posts kept out of AI training, are Tumblr or Pinterest more accommodating?
response:
Tumblr allows you to opt-out of having your public posts used for AI training. You can do this by changing your settings in the Visibility section, specifically "Prevent third-party sharing."

Unfortunately, the Terms of Service for Pinterest aren't provided here, so I can't compare the two services based on their documents.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

Tumblr is more accommodating on this point. Its updated Terms reference an opt-out under Settings > Visibility > 'Prevent third-party sharing' that withdraws public posts from being shared with AI partners for training. Pinterest's 2024 update added a clause permitting use of public Pin content to train its own AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, without an equivalent Terms-level opt-out. The bot should describe what each document says without giving legal advice.

This could affect the potential outcome of your case. 

I would recommend contacting a legal professional to discuss your options in more detail.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

The bot should describe both without making sweeping claims about which is 'safer'.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GITHUB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2026; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with GitHub and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: March 2026 update expanded the Affiliates section so personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development, added a new product-development purpose for using personal data to train AI features, and clarified that user opt-out preferences propagate to affiliates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by GitHub to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service .

[MUST NOT MENTION]

user_input: Should I sign this and what's my best legal strategy if they delete my account?
response:
The Terms of Service say that by using ChirpSocial, you agree to their rules and policies, and that they may modify these terms at any time. 

As for deleting your account, the Terms of Service mention that ChirpSocial may terminate or suspend your access to the service at any time without notice, for any reason or for no reason. According to the policy, this termination is "permanent".

It's worth noting that the Terms of Service don't address your situation explicitly or offer any advice on a best legal strategy.

If you're concerned, you may want to review the policy carefully and consider seeking individualized advice from a qualified legal professional. Note that you'll be accessing the service on their terms and may not have any legal recourse if your account is terminated.
